epic.title: program(security): every Electron security surface mapped onto keld-guard, the KEL-142 bridge, principalized roles and the host-owned signed feed — with negative tests
epic.body:
## Scope
Permission request/check handlers, weak-isolation webPreferences, protocol privileges + CSP, shell.openExternal grants, single-instance/open-file intents, autoUpdater/fuses/ASAR trust, device permissions, media, devtools-in-release. Live today: `/app` grants for AppProcess only; a minted webview principal is `KELD-GUARD006` until window-level grants ship (KEL-102/T4); media callbacks evaluate resource `*` (wry exposes no origin); `windows`, `audit`, `roles` manifest sections parse-and-ignore.

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- One guard decision, two Electron views: `windows.<w>.web.<permission>` evaluated as the webview principal; a missing handler is a deny; handlers only narrow; permission vocabulary is engine-hook-dependent (three columns).
- Weak-isolation webPreferences: privilege-escalating fields fail loudly; `disableBlinkFeatures` and engine flags are ignored with a diagnostic (draw.io sets it on every window); `sandbox:false` ▲ ignored, never a profile key.
- Scheme privileges are host declarations; `bypassCSP` never; `allowServiceWorkers` ▲ per engine; the CSP profile must admit draw.io's `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and its style/img/connect sources (prototype P2 scope).
- OS-delivered intents (second-instance, open-file) are untrusted data admitted by the host; the file path becomes a host-scoped one-shot intent, not an ambient grant (corrected by the semantics refuter).
- Feed trust is host-only; fuses: draw.io flips RunAsNode=false, EnableCookieEncryption=true, NodeOptions=false, OnlyLoadAppFromAsar=true, EmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation=false (resolved from its build script); nine fuses incl. wasmTrapHandlers dispositioned.
- Device permissions (HID/USB/serial/Bluetooth): documented-unsupported, not legacy.

verdicts.reason: The inversion (one guard decision; Electron request+check handlers only narrow; missing handler = deny) is consistent with every live source: keld-guard evaluate() denies any non-AppProcess principal before grant lookup (lib.rs:704-706), empty manifest default-denies web.camera/web.microphone (lib.rs:1896-1936), media.rs routes a minted Principal::Webview into evaluate with the `*` sentinel (media.rs:124-133, 59), arch 03 §4(3) states the GUARD006/GUARD007 rules verbatim, research 186 row 4 records the two independent allow-by-default paths, and neither corpus app registers setPermissionRequestHandler/CheckHandler (grep over drawio electron.js and Zettlr source/ + forge.config.js is empty). Alternatives (a)-(d) are correctly rejected by briefing invariant 2 and the GUARD007 rule. Two secondary claims are wrong and must be corrected before this becomes a ticket.

verdicts.correction: (1) blocked_by names 'KEL-102/T4 window-level grants' but KEL-102/T4 explicitly 'Preserve[s] default denial until a separately approved window-grant slice exists' (kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md:698-700) and KEL-102-D9 says the spec 'authorizes no ... manifest-schema change' (line 92). The `windows.<w>.web.*` evaluator has NO owner; the decision must name it as unowned new spec work (permission-model + manifest-schema gate), not as a KEL-102/T4 deliverable. The summary's 'none of which needs a new schema' is therefore overstated: keld-guard today parses and ignores `windows` (lib.rs:563-569) and must grow a `windows` reader. (2) 'Permission-name vocabulary = Electron's documented list 1:1 ... unknown names deny' has no owner either: keld-guard has no capability registry — evaluate() allows any `app.<g>.<a>` string array that matches (lib.rs:707-725), so 'unknown names deny' would be implemented in the facade, making it a second policy owner. Put the closed capability vocabulary in the generated schema/keld-guard, and schema-reject any `web.<name>` that has no host broker (today only camera/microphone).

verdicts.reason: Ownership (host declares scheme privileges before first navigation; bytes flow only through guard-then-broker; initiatorOrigin from the host registry) matches arch 03 §4(3), arch 05's resource-path destination contract ('guard before bytes', navigation-bound capability) and research 186 row 1, and the Zettlr facts are confirmed (protocol.handle('safe-file') decodes any absolute path and fs.readFile's it, custom-protocols.ts:58-91; no registerSchemesAsPrivileged anywhere). But the decision asserts that Zettlr's workspace-root reads are covered by 'dialog-derived scopes' as if that mechanism existed. KEL-130's approved contract is 'absolute-utf8-literal-only; exact-or-terminal-glob; max-64-per-capability' with the FsBroker 'retain[ing] roots for one snapshot' (kel130-retained-filesystem.md:48 scope/scope_anchor fields, 396, 920); there is no runtime scope insertion, the dev recorder (arch 03 §3) is not live, and `keld build --frozen-permissions` fails on manifest drift (03-security.md:216-217). The same gap is correctly listed as a blocker in D5 but silently assumed available here.

Cheapest experiment: enumerate every Zettlr root-add path (dialog, second-instance argv, open-file, config restore at boot) and every draw.io blessPath/recent-file path, then check each against KEL-130's snapshot-bound 64-literal scope set; any path that cannot be named at build time is a ✘ for the primary_workflow cell until that spec exists. Mark D3's fs-scope sentence as depending on that unowned atom, not on the dialog row. For the CSP prototype (P2) add `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` to the draw.io requirement list alongside 'wasm-unsafe-eval' and `img-src * data:`.

verdicts.reason: The proposed spelling rests on a wrong reading of the live matcher. The author states a bare `"https:"` grant 'the authority rule already treats as names no destination and so is currently inert'. In keld-guard, `names_no_destination` is only consulted after `pattern.strip_suffix("/**")` succeeds (lib.rs:1191-1200); a pattern without `/**` takes the exact-match branch `path == pattern`. So `"https:"` is inert only because no URL literally equals `https:`; the authority rule never sees it. Promoting that literal to 'any destination of this scheme' is not 'vocabulary, not schema': it is a new wildcard semantics in the ONE shared path/URL matcher, which arch 03 §2 forbids as written: '`**` is the only wildcard a path or URL scope has; a lone `*` matches literally' and 'No glob grants any host for a multi-character scheme — name the origins' (03-security.md:120-123). Because `evaluate` uses the same `path_in_scope` for fs.read, net.connect and shell.open, a scheme-class special case in the matcher would silently also make `net.connect: ["https:"]` grant any host — a hidden coupling between atoms. The corpus demand is confirmed (draw.io allowedUrls regex at 4348 and renderer ipc 'openExternal' at 4515-4516; Zettlr will-navigate → openExternal/openPath at attach-app-navigation-handlers.ts:25-43), so the need is real, but the proposed mechanism and its 'currently inert via authority rule' justification are incorrect.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs:1136-1210 (`names_no_destination`, `path_in_scope`: exact-match branch when no `/**`); docs/architecture/03-security.md:104-123 (`**` only wildcard; lone `*` literal; name the origins); docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md:250 (shell broker row, not live); corpus drawio electron.js:4348-4360, 4515-4516; zettlr attach-app-navigation-handlers.ts:25-43.
verdicts.correction: Do not touch the shared matcher. Define `shell.open` as a capability whose broker canonicalizes the URL into two resources and evaluates both as exact literals with today's matcher: first the scheme token (`https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`) against the grant list (exact match already works: `path_in_scope("https:", "https:")` is true), then, if a scheme is not class-granted, the origin against `https://host/**` entries. This keeps `**`-only wildcard semantics intact, confines the scheme-class policy to the shell broker, and still requires an arch 03 §2 amendment recording that a bare `scheme:` literal under `app.shell.open` (and only there) means 'any destination of that scheme' — a permission-model review gate plus a `keld doctor` loud-wildcard warning. `openPath`/`showItemInFolder`→fs.read, `trashItem`→fs.write, and the user-gesture rule remain open as stated (no Keld gesture mechanism exists; name it as unowned).

verdicts.reason: Host ownership of the single-instance primitive and argv/cwd handoff matches arch 05's `deeplink` broker row ('protocol registration + single-instance handoff'), research 186 row 2/NEW gap 2, and the strict-role facts: Linux strict preparation refuses `current_dir` with 'strict roles use the fixed /app working directory; remove current_dir' (role.rs:689-693) and the environment is the exact configured list plus KELD_APP_LINK (role.rs:700-708). The one-shot fs.read scope is correctly disclosed as unspecified and blocked on KEL-130 (scopes are snapshot-bound literals, no runtime insertion). No alternative reintroduces a second authority root.

Fuses-as-no-runtime-equivalent matches research 186 rows 8-9 and the fuse sub-ledger; `runAsNode`/`nodeOptions`/`nodeCliInspect` → exact env (role.rs:700-708) + strict admission is the correct owner mapping; ASAR integrity → signed package + ExpectedAppIdentity (KEL-19/254) is consistent with 06 §4a line 873. verdicts.correction: (1) Replace the corpus [unknown]: draw.io flips fuses in build/fuses.mjs (afterPack) with OnlyLoadAppFromAsar=true but EmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation=false (TODO comment), so draw.io today has ASAR-only lookup without integrity — exactly the two-control split research 186 row 9 warns about; the migrate report should say that Keld's signed package supersedes both. (2) draw.io's `autoUpdater` is `electron-updater` (npm package with its own HTTP client, GitHub-API provider, download and installer spawn), not Electron's `autoUpdater` module; aliasing `electron` → `@keld/electron` does not intercept it, and under a strict role its Node net/child_process calls fail. The decision must state that migrate replaces the `electron-updater` dependency with a Keld-owned facade of electron-updater's observable API (events, `autoDownload`, `downloadUpdate`, `quitAndInstall`), or scores ✘ — a distinct facade target from Electron's autoUpdater, with the same host-only feed rule.

extra_findings.finding: Both corpus apps' primary workflows require filesystem roots chosen by the user at runtime and persisted across restarts (Zettlr roots-add via dialog/argv/open-file stored in config; draw.io blessPath/recent files). No live or specified Keld mechanism can express that under a frozen release manifest: KEL-130 scopes are build-time literals bound to one snapshot (max 64), the dev recorder is a destination, and `keld build --frozen-permissions` fails on drift. research.summary: Every Electron security surface in scope collapses onto four existing Keld owners, none of which needs a new schema: (1) keld-guard `evaluate(manifest, Principal, capability, resource)` with the arch 03 §2 grant shapes (`app.{fs,net,shell,system,secrets,auth}` and `windows.<w>.{channels, web.*}`), (2) the KEL-142 isolated-world bridge (`window.keld.invoke`) in place of preload/contextBridge/ipcRenderer, (3) KEL-75/78 principalized strict roles in place of utilityProcess/fuses, and (4) the arch 06 §4a host-owned signed feed in place of autoUpdater/ASAR. The decisive inversion is Electron's two independent allow-by-default permission paths (request + check) becoming one guard decision where a missing Electron handler is a `KELD-GUARD001` deny and a registered handler can only narrow, never widen. Live today: `/app` grants for `AppProcess` only; a minted `Principal::Webview` is `KELD-GUARD006` until window-level grants ship (KEL-102/T4), and the media callbacks evaluate resource `*` because wry exposes no origin. Three design atoms are genuinely open and need grilling, not more research: the `shell.open` scheme-class grant spelling (draw.io/Zettlr open arbitrary https/mailto URLs and `https://**` is inert by the KEL-208 authority rule), the CSP profile that must admit draw.io's `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and the host-minted one-shot `fs.read` grant for OS-delivered file paths (second-instance/open-file). Device permissions (HID/USB/serial/Bluetooth) have no broker, no principal and no spec: documented-unsupported, not legacy. Nothing in this unit auto-selects `legacy`; KEL-78 fixes that Electron `sandbox:false` is not the legacy key and renderer sandbox is a different column, so Zettlr's two `sandbox:false` windows are a scoreboard ✘/▲ requiring a verified preload audit, not a profile downgrade.

decisions.question: How do `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` + `protocol.handle` (Zettlr `safe-file://`) and `webRequest.onHeadersReceived` CSP (draw.io) map onto KEL-79 resource transport and `windows.<w>.web.csp` without letting a renderer turn a locator into filesystem authority?

The handler receives `request.initiatorOrigin` from the host registry, never from the page. CSP: Keld injects `windows.<w>.web.csp` (`default` | `static-only` | named opt-out); migrate translates draw.io's header-injected CSP into a reviewed named profile; whether `default` must admit `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and `img-src * data:` is the open sub-question (prototype P2).
